title: CoW Protocol GPv2Settlement — GlueX/CIP-55 solver-allowance surface (live but not drainable)
closed_reasons: All live spenders are msg.sender-bound standard routers/pools (UniswapV2Router02, SwapRouter/SwapRouter02, AggregationRouterV3/V4/V5, ZeroEx, Paraswap TokenTransferProxy/AugustusSwapper, Balancer Vault, DODO, PancakeRouter, DXswapRouter, ~60 Curve/Vyper pools)
Balancer Vault swap/batchSwap are gated by authenticateFor(funds.sender) (fork-verified revert)
CowExecutor (0x2FbB05d2, 0xf3fc03f5) value paths are onlyCowSettlementContract (source + fork-verified revert)
Solver helper 0x1d94BedC validates msg.sender is a genuine Uniswap V3 pool -> reverts 'UNIV3R: bad pool' (fork-verified); payer is the entry msg.sender
Solver helper 0x0500001f direct uniswapV3SwapCallback call does not move settlement funds (fork-verified)
RFQ venues (KyberSwapRFQ, BebopSettlement, current HashflowRouter 0x55084ee0, SwapFacade, AirSwap Swap) require a maker/MM signature over the order and use msg.sender as taker

GPv2Settlement's own fund-moving entries (settle, swap) are onlySolver; setPreSignature/invalidateOrder are owner-bound; freeFilledAmountStorage/freePreSignatureStorage are onlyInteraction; simulateDelegatecall* revert by construction
Users approve GPv2VaultRelayer, whose transferFromAccounts is onlySettlement
2023 SwapGuard 0xcd07a769 holds no live allowance for any held token; 0xc0e82c1e (2023 attacker contract) has empty code
key_facts: The settlement owns 221,541 Approval logs (owner=GPv2Settlement) across 104 distinct spenders and 2,532 distinct tokens, blocks 12,959,355..15,450,000+ (pass5's claim of 'no settlement-owned approvals found' is WRONG)
399 (spender, token) pairs are LIVE today across 72 spenders: allowance(settlement, spender) > 0 AND settlement balanceOf(token) > 0
Settlement buffer at block 26,253,971 = $2,931.92 (DefiLlama prices); excludes unpriced imBTC (0.00132) and SLP (50,142) => ~$3.0k

Legacy HashflowRouter 0xF6a94dfD0E6ea9ddFdFfE4762Ad4236576136613 is still live/unpaused with a max allowance from the settlement and executes baseToken.transferFrom(quote.trader, ...) from a calldata field BEFORE the MM-signature check (fork-verified: the pull executes; tx reverts without a valid quote)
The current HashflowRouter 0x55084ee0 uses transferFrom(_msgSender(), ...) - the legacy deployment is the unhardened one; this is the exact 2023 CoW-hack helper/mechanism (trader = settlement)
Direct attacker transferFrom(settlement, ...) reverts; the approved-spender control test shows an approved spender CAN pull the buffer (latent-risk model)
17/17 fork tests pass at block 26,253,971; no mainnet transactions
caveats: The legacy-Hashflow vector is conditional: it needs an authorised market maker to sign a quote naming the settlement as `trader` (the 2023 attacker did exactly this via the public RFQ API). Not provable read-only => unproven, medium confidence.

The global approval sweep covered 0-15.5M blocks plus per-token sweeps of every token the settlement holds; the 15.5M->head global sweep was truncated by RPC/DNS flakiness, so an unseen spender could exist in that window (bounded by the per-token sweeps).
imBTC and SLP are unpriced (illiquid/deprecated); the buffer total is a lower bound by that amount.
The buffer is volatile block-to-block (observed ~$1.5k and ~$2.9k within hours) due to solver internalisation and daily fee sweeps.
No transactions were sent; everything is read-only fork/source analysis.
one_liner: External unprivileged attacker can extract ~$0 live from CoW GPv2Settlement: the settlement owns ~400 live token allowances to ~104 spenders (a far larger surface than pass5 reported) but every one is msg.sender-bound, auth-gated or signature-gated, fork-verified; the only residual is a live max allowance to the legacy Hashflow router 0xF6a94dfD, whose tradeRFQT pulls from the calldata `trader` field before the MM-signature check (conditional on an MM-signed quote naming the settlement).
